rule: Top-level / file-level code (outside any function or type): the caller is the file's module ID. | Languages without one (Ruby, PHP, C, C++, ObjC, Zig file scope) use the file path below the scan root without extension (`lib/devise/rails/routes`). | An empty caller or `<global>` is a wrong caller.
source: KNOWN_GAP: calls in file-level const initializers and some decl-literal forms (return .init(), .field = .x()) are not emitted
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a free function (`file.f`, `std.x.f`) is `direct`. All files sit directly under src/, so the file qualifier is the basename (`app`, `util`). The initializers of the file-scope consts `table_size` and `default_point` are file-level code (outside any function or type); SPEC names Zig file scope among the languages whose top-level caller is the file path below the scan root without extension → caller `app`. No implicit edge: Zig has no <clinit>/<init>. This case covers the first half of the gap; 11-decl-literal-calls covers the second.
